newsitem.title: INDIA: India's navy on charm offensive in Kashmir.
newsitem.headline: India's navy on charm offensive in Kashmir.

text.p: India is taking an unsual measure in its drive to end separatist militancy in Kashmir -- it is wooing youths from the landlocked region into the navy.

Commodore S. Nath said the navy had decided to ease the examination requirements for recruits from the mountainous region, where more than 20,000 people have died in insurgency-related violence since a revolt erupted in 1990.

Local news agencies quoted Nath on Sunday as saying a recruitment drive would be held in the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir state, Srinagar, in July. The state is mostly Hindu India's only Moslem-majority province.

Tens of thousands of soldiers are stationed in the Kashmir valley to combat insurgency. Separatist leaders regularly accuse the army of violating human rights. Government officials say perpetrators of violations are punished.
